notes_markdown:
**A diagnostic log that narrates what culler did, safer server
re-renders, and a confirm before Match Look throws aligned work away.**
The server-side fixes came out of one live session on a real aligned
series, with the new log open beside the app.

- **Match Look asks before throwing work away.** `Esc` on an untouched
  session still leaves at once, but once anything is matched or aligned
  it arms instead — "press Esc again to discard 4 aligned photos" — and
  only a second `Esc` discards. Any other key or click stands down (and
  still does its own job), `M` commits as ever, and the sidebar's `Esc`
  hint shows the count before you ever press it.
- **A diagnostic log, always on.** `~/.culler/logs/culler.log` records
  what culler did — the photo you focused and everything it knew about
  it, each edit, each step of a `J`, each server hiccup — one line per
  event, rotated at 8 MB. Send its tail with a bug report; launch with
  `--verbose` to watch it live in a terminal.
- **`J` asks before replacing an edit with a plain render.** On a photo
  that already fronts a culler edit, a `J` with no grade and no crop
  loaded (the state after a server read that came back empty) used to
  bake the RAW plain over your edit — an aligned series lost a frame
  that way. It now arms first ("press J again") and only a second `J`
  runs it; any other key stands it down.
- **Your grade survives a restart even when the server save failed.**
  After a `J` the photo's develop and crop now follow it into culler's
  own state file, so a restart with an empty or unreachable server
  copy still shows — and bakes — the edit you made. When the server
  save fails, every later upload says so until you restart culler.
- **Album views find the RAW.** A photo whose server stack holds the
  RAW now develops and re-renders from it even when the album only
  contains the render; `J` used to refuse there with "its stack carries
  none".
- **A grade and its crop can no longer lose each other.** Committing a
  crop on a photo whose grade had come from the server used to leave a
  half-empty local record, so the next launch showed the crop without
  the grade (or the reverse) and a `J` would have baked it that way.
  culler now fills the missing half from the server copy, keeps the
  local record whole, and saves the grade with **every** upload, not
  only when something changed since the last one.
